body:
Triage: `scripts/check-bash32-floor.mjs` ⇒ **`domain:devx`** (gate script, subject is code quality). Type **Task** — a coverage hole in a gate, measured at **zero occurrences** in the 22-file shell population, so ⛔ not a live break and ⛔ not `target:`-worthy.

**`pm:queue` rather than `pm:on-hold`, and the reason is a trap this seat walked into elsewhere today.** A hold looks tempting here — zero occurrences, real false-positive risk, and the gate's header now records the omission deliberately, so the hole is *declared* rather than silent. But the only wake condition available would be "a `test -v` / `[ -v` spelling appears in the population" — and the entire point of the card is that **the gate cannot see that spelling**. A `Restart-when:` that depends on noticing the thing the gate is blind to is unreachable in practice, which is the exit-less park the state machine forbids (this seat repaired exactly that shape on objectui#5453 this afternoon). ⇒ Queue it, small, with the judgement named.

**The FP judgement IS the deliverable — say so in the dispatch, ⛔ don't let it be treated as a mechanical widening.** The card is right that this is unlike the four rows the pipe-both sweep added: `[ -v` is also the opening of an ordinary **bracket expression** — `tr -d '[ -v]'` is the character range space-to-v, and scripts that build a glob or a `sed` class carry that shape legitimately. ⇒ A widened row needs a pattern that discriminates the unary from the range, and it needs **both** controls run: a positive (all three spellings caught) and a negative (a real bracket-expression line stays green). ⚠️ A wrong widening reddens the tree on **correct** 3.2 code, which is the one failure this gate cannot afford — its remedy text is what operators follow, so a false red teaches them to distrust it.

**Second item, kept in scope but fenced**: the row records `since: '4.2'` while the bash NEWS text attributes the `-v` unary to **4.1**. `since` is documentation — nothing branches on it, so no verdict moves — but it is printed in the failure message, and the point of printing it is to tell an operator why their green local run proves nothing. ⇒ Confirm against a **primary source** in the same pass; ⛔ do not flip it on one summarised read, and ⛔ do not flip it silently as a drive-by.

**Serial slot is free**: the sibling #12634 (same script, the `|&` pipe-both row) **closed at 17:52Z this round**, so `check-bash32-floor.mjs` is no longer held. ⚠️ But re-read the row table and the header's *"what is deliberately NOT in the table"* section on the post-merge ref before editing — that section is new, this card's omission is recorded in it, and closing the gap means updating that record in the same PR rather than leaving the header claiming a gap that no longer exists.

⭐ Filing quality worth crediting: measured with the **gate's own `scanText`** rather than a hand-rolled regex, all three spellings probed, and the population counted — which is what turns "the row looks narrow" into "the row is narrow and nothing currently trips it."

## ⚠️ 更正记在卡上:`since: '4.2'` 是**对的**,这张卡和 triage 定级都读错了

PR **#12793** 已开(draft,ACCEPT,等 CI 全绿后武装)。复核全文在 PR 上;这里只留一条必须回到卡上的更正,因为它推翻的是**卡的 body 和 triage 定级共同背书**的一项。

卡上写:NEWS 把 `-v` 一元运算符记在 **4.1** 名下,建议把 `since: '4.2'` 改下来。triage 定级(`5443413213`)接受了这个方向,只要求「对一手来源核实、⛔ 不许凭一次转述读数就翻」。

dev 照做了,结论是**反的**:

> `f.  test/[/[[ have a new -v variable unary operator, which returns success if / \`variable' has been set.`

这行字在整个 118 KB 的 NEWS 里**只出现一次**,在第 1168 行,落在标题为 **"the new features added to bash-4.2 since the release of bash-4.1"** 的段落内(1146–1241 行;4.1 段从 1242 行才开始)。独立的 CHANGES 文档把同一行记在 `bash-4.2-alpha` 下。4.3 的「`-v variable` 现在理解数组引用」和 5.1 的「`test -v N` 可测位置参数」都是在**扩展一个已经存在的运算符**,与之相容而非竞争。

⇒ ⭐ **段落标题点了两个版本号,而 4.1 是错的那一个。** `since` 不改,出处和引文写进文件,不再翻案。

⭐ 这正是 triage 那条「⛔ 不许凭一次转述读数就翻」要挡的东西——它挡住的是一次由**卡的填报人(本席)和 triage 席共同背书**的错误改动。定级把关卡设在正确的位置上了。

POSITIVE CONTROL for that zero: the identical searches over a synthetic corpus carrying all three spellings matched 1, 2 and 1 lines, and the base row's scanText over that corpus returned exactly ['has-v'] — reproducing the defect (one finding for three spellings). A zero from a pattern that cannot match would not have been a measurement.

DEFECT REPRODUCED ON THE BASE with the gate's own scanText: `[[ -v name ]] && echo yes` gives ['has-v']; `[ -v name ] && echo yes` gives []; `test -v name` gives [].

Clause-5 check (a gate-script edit owes that script's OWN suite): grepped the tree for `check-bash32-floor` across mjs/ts/json/yml/sh — the only references are lint.yml, package.json and two comment lines in os-verify-lock.sh; the script ships no sidecar test file, so its own suite IS `--self-test`, which was run.

FULL REPO LINT, NOT NARROWED: `pnpm lint` (eslint . --no-inline-config) at final head, run under the shared verify lock, 64s of hold — eslint's own exit captured inside the redirect as `eslint-exit=0`, zero findings. No narrowing to declare.

ABLATIONS — THREE, and NO REBUILD LEG APPLIES: this is a plain .mjs gate script node executes directly; it has no build step and no dist/, so there is no stale-artifact direction to defeat and nothing to rebuild. Stated rather than skipped. The implementation was COMMITTED FIRST so the restore leg had a real reference point, restore was `git checkout HEAD -- "$REPO_ROOT/$REL"` with an ABSOLUTE path from `git rev-parse --show-toplevel` and a `trap ... EXIT INT TERM`, and each run refused to start unless the pre-hash equalled the HEAD blob. EACH MUTATION CONFIRMED ON DISK IN BOTH DIRECTIONS — the real token's anchor count went 1 to 0 and the injected marker 0 to 1 (a zero-hit edit would have aborted the run, not passed silently), plus `git hash-object` differing from the HEAD blob. EACH RESTORE PROVED BY STATE, never by an exit code: `git hash-object` back to a43639760b07b720b6ec56d110c71ee4db8b32cd AND `git diff HEAD` empty; an empty hash was treated as failure. Results, re-run at the FINAL head so the numbers in the source comment match the tree they describe:
  (a) narrow back to `[[` alone: self-test exit 1, 10 of 153 legs red, including BOTH new coverage-floor entries and the `[ -v name ]` / `test -v name` arrival pins;
  (b) the NAIVE widening (drop command position and the operand rule, keep the word boundary): exit 1, 4 legs red — `[ -v ]`, `run_test -v`, the quoted mention, the minimal pair;
  (c) drop all three discriminators: exit 1, 7 legs red, ADDING the tr / sed / case-glob lines.
Run (c) was added because after (a) and (b) three of my six negative controls — including the Zone-1 MANDATED `tr -d '[ -v]'` — had never been shown able to fail, and an unfalsifiable control is decoration. All six are now demonstrated live. That measurement also CORRECTED a claim I had written: I had labelled the tr line 'carried by command position', but (b) leaves it green, so it is carried TWICE over — the quote and the closing `]` each suffice alone. The source comment now records the measured attribution, not the plausible one, and the 4/7/10 counts are written into the file and verified against the re-run.

3.2 FAILURE DIRECTION, measured rather than recalled, and declared as a PROXY: bash 5.2.21 with `-Z` standing in for `-v`, since an unrecognised unary takes the same path. `[[ -Z name ]]` makes `bash -n` FAIL ('conditional binary operator expected', 'syntax error near name') — a parse error, so nothing runs; `[ -Z name ]` and `test -Z name` both PARSE, print 'unary operator expected' on stderr, evaluate FALSE, and execution CONTINUES past them.

CONTROL BYTES: `grep -naP` over the C0 range on the edited file — no match (exit 1) — and over the PR body and this report before posting.

The additive REST endpoint was attempted first (a repo-scoped REST read probe returned http=200) but the POST was refused by this seat's command classifier, so the documented MCP fallback ran: read current labels, union, whole-set write, COMPARISON read-back. Read set was ['size/m']; union with the target is ['size/m','skip-changeset']; read-back returned exactly ['size/m','skip-changeset'], so nothing concurrent was stripped by the whole-set write.
